Dapple Weave is a concept meaning an alternating arrangement of coarse and fine filter threads. Fine Lattice is a concept meaning a supporting grid beneath the filter threads. Dapple Weave requires Fine Lattice. A filter with alternating coarse and fine threads over a supporting grid is an example of Dapple Weave. A filter with only coarse threads is a counterexample of Dapple Weave.

Thistle Spareband is a concept meaning a spare strip reserved beyond a planned cut. Ochre Cutreserve is another name for that same concept. Quartz Sidecast is a different concept meaning a deliberate sideways shift of a cutting guide. Thistle Spareband is the same concept as Ochre Cutreserve. Thistle Spareband is distinguished from Quartz Sidecast.

The skill named Amber contouring is the ability to trace two concentric contours.
The skill has application evidence only.
The skill concerns the cobalt panel.
The skill was demonstrated in Meadow workshop.
The recorded outcome of the skill is Dune inspection.
The skill was last validated on 2026-04-11.
The framework named Contour comparison organizes comparisons before cutting.
Its purpose is to compare traced contours before cutting.
The framework includes the procedure named Contour pass.
A component of the framework is the panel mentioned above.
The framework assumes the panel is rigid.
The framework applies to that panel.
Its failure mode is that warped panels make the comparison unreliable.
The framework is being tested; it has not been adopted.
Contour pass is a procedure for inspecting paired contours.
Its step is to trace the inner contour before tracing the outer contour.
Its strategy is to compare both contours before cutting.
Its prerequisite is a clean panel.
The procedure applies to the same panel.
The procedure requires the skill described above.
Its success check is that the contours remain concentric.
Its failure mode is that a warped panel displaces the contour.
Its counterexample is cutting before comparison.
The procedure was last validated on 2026-04-12T10:15:00Z.
The procedure has the same recorded inspection outcome as the skill.
Its standard is to compare the paired contours before any cut.
Its exemplar is the workshop mentioned above.
